oneLiner: Won the ad-tech case, lost four straight months of stock performance: Search compounding 17% and Cloud 82% against a $195-205B capex bill and a market that has decided Google is losing the model race.
thesis: Distribution is still the moat: ~91% global search share, 2.5B monthly AI Overviews users, AI Mode past 1B MAU, and Search revenue accelerating to +17% despite three years of substitution fear.

Cloud is a second franchise: $24.8B in Q2 (+82%) at ~35% segment margin with a $514B backlog; Thomas Kurian says roughly three quarters of Cloud customers now use its AI products and spend about 50% above their original commitments.
The structural antitrust tail just got much shorter: on Sep 2, 2026 Judge Brinkema rejected every structural remedy in the ad-tech case, leaving Google Ad Manager intact.
Earnings quality caveat persists: Q2 GAAP EPS of $9.11 included roughly $99B of equity-stake marks (Anthropic at $124.3B, SpaceX); core EPS was about $2.85.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (reported Jul 22, 2026)
points: Revenue $119.8B, +24% YoY (beat); operating income $40.8B, +30%; operating margin 34% (+2pp).
Google Services $94.5B (+15%); Search ~$63.3B (+17%); YouTube ads $11.1B (+13%); subscriptions/platforms/devices $12.9B.
Cloud $24.8B (+82%); Cloud operating income $8.8B vs $2.8B a year ago; backlog $514B.
GAAP EPS $9.11 including ~$99B of equity gains (Anthropic, SpaceX); ex-gains ~$2.85 vs $2.89 consensus.
FY2026 capex raised to $195-205B with further growth flagged for 2027; the stock fell ~5% after hours on the hike.

segments: Search ~53% of revenue; Cloud ~21% (solidly profitable, $514B backlog); YouTube ads ~9%; subscriptions/devices ~11%; Other Bets under 1%.

Gemini monetization: AI Mode above 1B MAU; AI Overviews carry ads; AI Pro $19.99/mo and AI Ultra $249.99/mo; Gemini 3.8 Flash priced at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
competitive: Model cadence is now the bear case, not distribution: Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash on Sep 2 - its third Flash model in six weeks - plus a cybersecurity model for government and enterprise, but the Gemini 3.5 Pro flagship Sundar Pichai promised for June still had not shipped.
ChatGPT remains roughly 900M weekly actives; agentic browsers (Atlas, Comet) attack the Chrome funnel; Perplexity around 45M MAU.
Cloud share (Synergy, Q1 2026): AWS 28%, Azure 21%, Google 14% - but GCP grew 82% against Azure's ~40% and AWS's ~28%.

Antitrust: ad-tech structural remedies denied Sep 2, 2026; search remedies (finalized Dec 2025 - data sharing, one-year default-deal caps, no Chrome divestiture) remain on appeal with a DOJ cross-appeal seeking Chrome divestiture, DC Circuit late 2026 or early 2027.
moat: Search distribution at ~91% share, the Chrome and Android funnel, and the largest AI distribution surface in the world; Cloud adds a TPU and Gemini infrastructure advantage that Broadcom's own disclosures now quantify - a long-term agreement to supply multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually. The $124B Anthropic stake is optionality on a rival's success. With Ad Manager left intact, the ads stack stays vertically integrated.
risks: Capex escalation: $195-205B in 2026 and rising in 2027; depreciation and free-cash-flow compression if AI revenue lags the build.
Model-cadence perception: a promised June flagship still unshipped in September is the specific thing driving the derating, and Flash releases do not answer it.
Search-case tail risk survives: the DOJ cross-appeal keeps Chrome divestiture and Apple-deal termination alive, and the one-year cap on default deals injects annual renewal risk.

Ad-tech relief is not final: the Brinkema opinion is sealed pending redactions (Sep 16) with a joint proposed final judgment due Oct 2, 2026, and the behavioral remedies themselves are not yet public.
FTC is reported to be in the final stages of a YouTube consumer-protection investigation tied to account suspensions and content-policy disclosures (reported, unverified).
Earnings quality: $6.26 of Q2's $9.11 EPS was investment marks that can reverse.
catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings late Oct 2026, with 2027 capex framing.
Ad-tech final judgment due Oct 2, 2026 and the unsealed remedy opinion after Sep 16.
DC Circuit oral arguments on the search case, late 2026 or early 2027.
Gemini 3.5 Pro flagship ship date - the single cleanest sentiment catalyst.
pricedIn: About $342, roughly 16% below the $408.61 high, after a four-month losing streak - the longest since 2015 - and a 10%-plus decline in the past month alone. Around 22-23x forward is mid-range of the historical 18-24x band for a business growing 24%. The bear case has migrated from antitrust to product: the ad-tech breakup risk just disappeared and the stock did not re-rate, which says the market is discounting model-race position and $200B of capex, not legal risk. The debate: is a four-month drawdown in the cheapest AI mega-cap an entry point, or the market correctly pricing the first sustained cadence gap versus OpenAI and Anthropic?

scenarios.bear: Capex tops $205B and rises again while Cloud decelerates into a capacity glut; depreciation crushes margins; the flagship model keeps slipping and query share finally cracks as agentic browsers route around Chrome; the DC Circuit reinstates structural search remedies; Anthropic marks reverse. Mid-teens multiple on lower core EPS.
scenarios.base: Search grows low double digits with AI Overviews monetizing near parity; Cloud compounds 40-60% off a $514B backlog; the ad-tech judgment is entered as behavioral-only and the search appeal drags through 2027; low-20s forward P/E on mid-teens core EPS growth grinds the stock higher between capex headlines.
scenarios.bull: A credible flagship ships and resets the narrative; Cloud sustains 60%+ with margin expansion; capex proves supply-constrained rather than speculative; Gemini layers ads and subscriptions into a second multi-tens-of-billions stream; both antitrust cases end behavioral, and the multiple re-rates toward 26-28x.

valPresets.note: Valuation basis is forward earnings: TTM FCF is crushed by the $195-205B capex program and TTM GAAP earnings are inflated by roughly $99B of Anthropic and SpaceX marks, so forward EPS is the cleanest anchor.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Jul 22). Revenue $119.8B, +24% (beat); operating income $40.8B (+30%), margin 34% (+2pts). Search $63.3B (+17%), YouTube ads $11.1B (+13%), Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B of segment profit versus $2.8B a year ago and a $514B backlog. GAAP EPS was $9.11, but roughly $99B of Anthropic and SpaceX equity marks sit inside it; core EPS was about $2.85 against $2.89 consensus. The disclosure that matters most: Cloud backlog of $514B is more than four times trailing Cloud revenue, which is the only number that makes a $200B capex program look like a supply response rather than a bet.
guidanceProse: FY2026 capex stands at $195-205B, raised from $180-190B, with further growth flagged for 2027. The legal picture improved sharply after the quarter: on Sep 2, 2026 Judge Brinkema rejected the DOJ's structural ad-tech remedies - no AdX divestiture, no open-sourcing of DFP auction logic, no contingent DFP divestiture - and accepted behavioral remedies instead, leaving Ad Manager integrated and the take rate unchanged. The opinion is sealed pending redactions on Sep 16, with a jointly proposed final judgment due Oct 2. The search case remains on appeal, where the DOJ cross-appeal still seeks Chrome divestiture.
